info.bio:
Screaming Trees se crea cuando unos compañeros de instituto deciden reunirse para tocar juntos después de fallidos intentos anteriores con otros grupos. El nombre proviene de un pedal de distorsión para guitarras. Al poco de su formación graban su primer EP, Other Worlds, publicado en SST Records, pero que salió a la venta después de su primer LP, titulado Clairvoyance y distribuido por Velvetone Records en 1986.

Un año después publican su segundo LP

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Managed by Susan Silver (1983)
podcast.body: Screaming Trees were an early client of Susan Silver, who started managing bands in Seattle in 1983 while still majoring in Chinese at the University of Washington. This management role predated her work with Soundgarden and Alice in Chains.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Singles Soundtrack Contribution (1992)
podcast.body: Songs from The Screaming Trees were played on the radio and in alternative clubs throughout late 1992, following the release of *Singles*. The movie and its soundtrack were instrumental in expanding the reach and popularity of grunge music. "Songs from Allison Chains, Pearl Jam, The Screaming Trees and The Smashing Pumpkins were all played on the radio and in alternative clubs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Academic and Artistic Pursuits
podcast.body: Barrett Martin, the drummer for Screaming Trees and Mad Season, is described as highly intelligent, holding bachelor's and master's degrees in anthropology, linguistics, and ethnomusicology, and was an honor student. He also became a Zen artist. "Bachelors and master's degrees in anthropology, linguistics, and ethnomusicology, and an honor student."

podcast.title: Associated with Grunge Movement (Mid-90s)
podcast.body: Screaming Trees was grouped with other bands like Stone Temple Pilots and Soundgarden under the Grunge umbrella, dominant in North America in the early and mid-90s. "We also had the Stone Temple pilots in screaming trees, Allison Chains, Mud Honey, Tad, and a ton of others who were all placed under the same Grunge umbrella."

podcast.title: Josh Homme as Touring Guitarist
podcast.body: Josh Homme toured as the rhythm guitarist for Screaming Trees for two years. He played with them at Lollapalooza in 1996 and was noted as a "six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist." "If you were at Lollapalooza in 1996 and saw the tree set, that six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist was Josh Hommie."

xref.title: First Management Client (1981) – The U-Men
xref.body: Susan Silver began her career in artist management by managing The U-Men, a Seattle group formed in 1981 that predated the widespread Grunge movement by a couple of years. She also managed Screaming Trees before taking on Soundgarden. "Silver got her start managing the U-Men, a Seattle group that predated the whole Grunge thing by a couple of years in 1981."

xref.title: Hiro Yamamoto's Departure (1989) – Pursuit of Education
xref.body: In 1989, bassist Hiro Yamamoto left Soundgarden to finish his master's degree in physical chemistry. After leaving the band, he continued his musical pursuits by playing in a band called Truly, which included members of Screaming Trees. "In 1989, there was a lineup change when bass player Hero Yamamoto quit to finish his master's degree in physical chemistry."

xref.title: Soundgarden Breakup (1997) – Tension from Manager/Wife Susan Silver and Separate Tour Transport
xref.body: The band broke up in 1997 partly due to the unresolvable conflict of interest created by Cornell being married to Susan Silver, who was also the band's manager (and the manager of Alice in Chains and Screaming Trees). By the end of the band's existence, each member was reportedly traveling separately by their own bus or plane between shows. After the divorce in 2002, Cornell filed a complaint with the California Labor Commission in 2006 alleging Silver had performed booking work without the required talent agent's license, and sought return of money she made from Soundgarden activities in 2005. "No conflict of interest there."

xref.title: Attempt to Revive Gamma Ray
xref.body: After his work with Screaming Trees and the first Desert Sessions, Josh Homme considered resurrecting his Gamma Ray project for a new long-term endeavor. However, a German power metal band already held the name and threatened legal action, forcing him to choose a different name. "His first thought was to resurrect gamma ray, but there was a problem. A German power metal band had dibs on that name and started making noises about legal action."

xref.title: Brief Stints with Grunge and Indie Bands
xref.body: For a period, Donna Dresch played with "the guys," including a stint as a member of the Seattle grunge band Screaming Trees and touring Australia playing bass for Dinosaur Jr. These experiences highlight her diverse musical background before forming Team Dresch. "Donna was a member of Seattle Grunge Ben Screaming Trees for a bit and toured Australia playing bass for dinosaur junior."

xref.title: Challenging Band Dynamics
xref.body: The band comprised Mike McCready (recovering alcoholic and drug addict), John Baker Saunders (who also had addiction issues), Layne Staley (Alice in Chains frontman, notorious drug addict), and Barrett Martin (Screaming Trees drummer, noted for his stability and academic background). Despite the varied personal struggles, the band managed to function. "Singing for the band was lain stately of Alice and Chains, a guy who had a reputation as being the biggest drug addict in a city of drug addicts."

xref.body: Josh Homme spent two years touring as the rhythm guitarist for the Seattle band Screaming Trees after meeting their singer Mark Lanegan, a Kyuss fan. He was described as a six-foot-five red-haired rhythm guitarist during their Lollapalooza 1996 set. "Mark was a fan of Kaya's and needed someone to tour with the trees and ask Josh if he would like to be his guitarist. So he did that for two years. If you were at Lollapalooza in 1996 and saw the tree set, that six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist was Josh Hommie."
